title: GoTu survey data: Income satisfaction is higher with temp work, but so is burnout
html:
Higher income satisfaction existing alongside higher burnout, fewer recent raises, and less access to paid time off makes it difficult to measure the value of flexible work through any one metric. A dental professional may place greater value on income, schedule flexibility, or control over when and where they work while accepting fewer of the benefits that can be associated with permanent employment. Compensation and benefit trends also changed over the course of GoTu’s surveys and will be explored separately in this series.

How dental professionals view their careers

How dental professionals choose to work may also be connected to how they view their careers. Hygienists working blended schedules reported slightly higher intent to remain in dental hygiene long term, although the difference was not statistically significant. The findings provide another reason to consider temporary and blended work as more than something dental professionals do while looking for a permanent position. For some, combining different work arrangements may simply be how they choose to build a career in dentistry.

For practices competing for employees, these findings expand the conversation around recruitment and retention. Hourly compensation remains an important part of employment decisions, but dental professionals may also be considering schedule flexibility, benefits, stability, workplace experience, and control over when and where they work. Understanding how employees prioritize those factors becomes more important when greater satisfaction in one area, such as income, does not necessarily translate to greater satisfaction across the rest of their work experience.

GoTu’s survey population is particularly familiar with flexible work. Across professions and survey years, 79% to 92% of respondents reported having performed temporary work at some point. (Note: This is for assistants and hygienists only.) Their experience provides a view into a segment of dentistry that has already had considerable exposure to different ways of working and may offer an early look at how dental professionals are combining permanent and temporary employment.
